title: Bridge Operator Cheatsheet and Customer Brief Library
author: Priya Anand
body:
Overview

Purpose: This page is a compact operational manual for the person who runs the incident bridge (Bridge Operator) and a curated library of customer-facing status and briefing templates. The goal is to accelerate correct first responses, keep stakeholders aligned, and provide well-structured customer communications that map to our SLO-driven severity model.

Quick reference (bridge operator role in one line)
- Own the incident bridge and high-level coordination until an Incident Commander (IC) or Service Owner is designated. Keep the bridge focused, visible, and timed.

Incident lifecycle (sprint-style stages)
1) Detect & Acknowledge (0-5m): Alert fires -> bridge opened -> initial triage started.
2) Stabilize & Communicate (5-30m): Contain blast radius, identify impacted services/customers, publish initial customer notice.
3) Repair & Verify (30m-6h): Work on root cause mitigation, apply fixes, smoke test.
4) Restore & Monitor (6h-72h): Restore full traffic and performance, watch for regressions.
5) Review (48h-14d): Post-incident analysis, RCA, action items, and follow-up communications.

Bridge operator responsibilities (concise checklist)
- Open the bridge (Zoom/Jitsi/Teams link) and pin it to the incident page.
- Create the incident ticket in Jira (template: "INC-Template") and set severity per SLO table below.
- Post an initial public status page entry (see templates) within 10 minutes for Sev 1/2.
- Add the incident to the daily incident tracker spreadsheet.
- Triage alerts into: infrastructure, runtime, data, or external dependency.
- Coordinate diagnostic runbooks and demand subject-matter experts (SMEs).
- Enforce meeting discipline: 10-minute standups for first hour, then 30–60 minute cadence.
- Capture timeline milestones and decisions for postmortem.

Fast triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1. Confirm alert validity (run quick evidence commands).
2. Determine impact scope: services, regions, customers, APIs.
3. Assign IC if not already assigned. If no IC within 8 minutes, Bridge Operator temporarily acts as IC for orchestration only.
4. Set severity using the SLO-driven chart.
5. Publish initial customer notice and internal #incident Slack channel post.

Containment checklist (10–60 minutes)
- Throttle or isolate offending endpoints (load balancer weight adjustments, route-based throttles).
- Apply traffic re-routing or failover to standby region if applicable.
- Implement temporary feature flags or circuit breakers to reduce error amplification.
- Increase logging level in targeted services for 30–60 minutes for evidence collection.

Restoration checklist (1–6 hours)
- Apply the minimal viable fix that restores customer-visible SLOs.
- Run health-check suite: smoke tests, critical path synthetic transactions, and latency histograms.
- Coordinate a staged rollback or progressive rollout for fixes to avoid regression.
- Prepare a customer-facing update with ETA and restored capabilities.

Post-incident and postmortem workflow
- Assign a Postmortem owner within 24 hours.
- Gather timeline, evidence artifacts (logs, spans, alerts), config diffs, and deployment history.
- Run blameless RCA: causal chain, contributing factors, and immediate/long-term mitigations.
- Create action items with owners and due dates; track in our ops backlog.
- Publish the postmortem to Confluence and notify relevant GTM/customer success reps.

On-call rotation and handoff rules (compact)
- Primary oncall covers 24/7 pager for first responder duties. Secondary covers escalation failures and cross-service incidents.
- Handoff checklist (to include in every rotation change): current active incidents, outstanding action items, ongoing game-day drills, and pager quiet windows.
- Shadow window: new oncall shadows outgoing oncall for 48 hours during first week on rotation.

Game day design (targeted drills for common failure modes)
Purpose: practice time-to-detect, bridge choreography, and cross-team coordination without customer impact.
Example drills:
- Multi-region failover: simulate region network partition and exercise automated failovers.
- Silent regression detection: subtle latency increase that crosses SLO after 2 hours.
- Downstream dependency blackhole: third-party auth provider returns 500s intermittently.
Metrics to measure per drill: Mean time to bridge (MTTB), Mean time to identify root cause (MTTRc), Mean time to restore (MTTR), communication latency (time to first customer notice).

Status page templates (short, copy/paste-ready)
Template A — Immediate (Sev 1/Sev 2, public):
- Title: Service degradation affecting API responses
- Body: We are investigating increased errors for text-generation API calls impacting customers in US-East. Engineers are on the bridge and we will post updates every 15 minutes.
- Impact: High — requests may see errors or elevated latency.
- Next update: in ~15 minutes

Template B — Follow-up (after containment):
- Title: Partial restoration of API throughput
- Body: We have contained the incident. Error rates have dropped by ~80% for most customers. A subset of long-running requests may still be degraded. Full restoration ETA: 2 hours.

Customer brief templates (tiered by severity)
Sev 1 Customer Brief (external-facing email):
- Subject: Incident impacting Redwood inference API — immediate notice
- Greeting: Hello <Customer Name>,
- Summary: At <time>, we detected a service disruption impacting inference requests in <region>.
- Impact: Describe affected endpoints and expected customer-visible behavior.
- Mitigation & ETA: What we have done and next update schedule.
- Contact: Primary CS rep and escalation contact.
- Closing: We apologize for the impact and appreciate your patience.

Sev 2 Customer Brief (less urgent, portal notice)
- Short title and bullet summary, root cause (once known), workaround instructions if available, and timeline for follow-up.

Alerting & evidence collection (commands & snippets)
- Standard log grep (Kubernetes): kubectl -n $NS logs -l app=$SERVICE --tail=200 | grep -i "error" | head -n 200
- Trace link pattern: open tracing UI: https://tracing.redwood.internal/trace/$TRACE_ID
- Quick histogram check (Promql): rate(http_request_errors_total[5m]) / rate(http_requests_total[5m]) > 0.02
- Example PagerDuty quick-ack command (CLI): pd incidents acknowledge --id $INCIDENT_ID --message "Acknowledged by bridge operator"

Ownership & escalation matrix (plain list)
- Bridge Operator: temporary orchestration, timeline capture, customer notices.
- Incident Commander (IC): tactical decision making and cross-team coordination.
- Service Owner: technical ownership for fixes and RCA.
- SRE Lead: postmortem quality and mitigation review.

SLOs & thresholds (table)
| Service area | SLO | Severity mapping |
|-------------|-----|-----------------|
| Text-generation API (prod) | 99.95% availability (30d) | >1% error budget burn/day -> Sev 2; >5% -> Sev 1 |
| Embeddings API | 99.9% availability (30d) | >0.5% error budget burn/day -> Sev 2; >2% -> Sev 1 |
| Console dashboards | 99% availability | degraded dashboards (no propagation) -> Sev 3 |

Runbook template (minimal, copyable)
- Title: <service> incident runbook
- Symptoms: <observed metrics and errors>
- Quick checks: topology, recent deploys, infra alarms
- Containment steps: <commands / toggles / rollbacks>
- Restore steps: <minimal fix / progressive rollout>
- Validation: <smoke tests / synthetic checks>
- Post-incident: timeline and evidence export commands

Appendix: example incident timeline skeleton (use in postmortem)
- 00:00 Alert triggered: <alert name>
- 00:02 Bridge opened by <name>
- 00:08 IC assigned: <name>
- 00:12 Initial public notice posted
- 00:30 Containment achieved: <measure>
- 02:00 Partial restoration observed
- 05:10 Full restoration confirmed

Appendix: evidence artifact checklist (what to attach to Jira)
- Alert graph snapshots (60m, 6h, 24h)
- Kibana/ES log export (correlated request IDs)
- Traces (sample trace ids)
- Deployment diffs and config rollbacks
- PagerDuty timeline export

Appendix: suggested post-incident email to internal stakeholders
Subject: Post-incident summary — <service> — <date>
Body: TL;DR, timeline, impact, root cause (draft), action items and owners, expected completion dates.

Bridge operator checklist quickcard (one-paragraph)
When an alert fires: open the bridge, confirm impact, assign an IC, publish a short status page entry, run the fast triage checklist, and ensure the incident ticket is created and linked to the bridge. Keep updates short and time-boxed. Capture all decisions and evidence so the Postmortem is straightforward.

Notes and references
- Related runbooks: link from "related_pages" above.
- When in doubt on severity, default to higher severity for customer-facing services and escalate to SRE Lead.
- Regularly rehearse this cheatsheet in game days and update after each drill to keep it accurate.
